subject: English
passage: Marine biologists Busra Toprak, Thanh Le, and Vadim Polishchuk cultivated colonies of Stylophora pistillata coral in samples of artificially acidified seawater—simulating projected ocean acidification levels—and, serving as a control group, in normal pH seawater. They found that while all the coral fragments initially survived, the skeletal growth of the acidified-water corals was significantly reduced compared with those in the control group. Moreover, unlike the corals in the control group, the acidified-water corals exhibited bleaching, decreased calcification rates, and compromised structural integrity—indicators of stress that were corroborated by postharvest genetic analysis.
prompt: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?

choices.A: It discusses the findings of a study that evaluated the effects of exposing a coral species to acidified seawater conditions.
choices.B: It describes an experiment that addressed an unresolved question about the extent to which acidified seawater resembles normal oceanic conditions.
choices.C: It compares two distinct methods of measuring indicators of stress in corals exposed to a simulated oceanic environment.
choices.D: It presents evidence in support of the hypothesis that coral survival in acidified oceans is an impossible outcome.

explanation: Choice A is the best answer. The text describes an experiment wherein marine biologists compared coral growth in normal and acidified seawater conditions. It then discusses the findings of the study, including the fact that all the fragments initially survived but that the corals grown in acidified water exhibited signs of stress.
